tagline: One county road, six names, across Russell County.
intro: Route 640 starts at St. Paul on the Clinch River and crosses Russell County toward Wardell under one number and half a dozen names, River Road, Reeds Valley, Middle Valley, Long Hollow, River Mountain and Clifton Farm roads.
It is also part of the Heart of Appalachia Bike Route. Along the way it runs by Castlewood, beside the Clinch, and passes near the county seat at Lebanon.

moments.title: St. Paul
moments.text: The town began in 1791 as a French Huguenot settlement overlooking the Clinch, and the remains of that settlement lie in the Sugar Hill section of Clinch River State Park.

moments.title: Castlewood
moments.text: Jacob Castle reportedly bought Castle's Woods from the Shawnee for a hound dog, a knife and a shot of whiskey, and the town incorporated in 1991 and undid it in 1997.

moments.title: Lebanon
moments.text: Lebanon was founded in 1818 to give Russell County a new county seat, and its Lutheran church was founded in 1851.
